purpose: Four visual chassis concepts; not CAD, fabrication or electrical validation
onboard_configuration: two rear independent gear drives, front passive steering, 4x63mm tires, Pi5, camera, IC5 2S battery and alimentation-r2 power hardware
common_prompt:
Use case: product-mockup / mechanical chassis concept study. Generate ONE high-resolution landscape engineering product illustration for a French DIY terrestrial robot project, on a clean warm-white studio background, 3/4 elevated front-left view showing the whole vehicle and open internal packaging. Crisp realistic CAD-style materials and believable component sizes, restrained neutral-grey structure, red motor housings and blue power components. The subject is a four-wheel indoor car robot, not a flying drone. Exactly FOUR black road tires, nominal diameter63mm width26mm, two front wheels passively steered by one small servo and tie rods, two rear wheels each driven independently by its OWN compact cylindrical brushless motor diameter24mm length36mm through its OWN two-stage spur gear reduction and shaft/bearing mounts. Two motors total, both at rear; two small finned ESCs near them. No front drive, no differential, no belt drive, no propellers, no six wheels, no monster truck tires, no speculative suspension.
Take all selected onboard hardware into account and give it believable space: a low black rectangular 139x46x25mm 2S hardcase battery with two retaining straps and accessible IC5 plug; a RaspberryPi5 board85x56mm with active cooler, USB leads, microSD and antenna edge clear of metal walls; a 25x25mm step-down regulator; a front USB board-camera with M12 lens on an adjustable bracket and clear forward view; rear Hall wheel sensors and protected small magnet locations; two long covered distribution bus bars roughly107x23mm EACH; one substantial solid-state power relay on an aluminium finned heatsink roughly85x52x41mm plus relay height, with free ventilation; a blue distribution block roughly69x30x46mm; an accessible red manual power-cutoff plunger on a black switch base; one cylindrical white main class-T fuse on a covered holder plus THREE smaller cylindrical white cartridge branch fuses on holders; terminal blocks and properly restrained wiring. Clearly segregate heavy red/black power cables from thin logic cables. Add a small empty mounting reservation for the future battery-monitoring PCB rather than inventing that circuit. Show routing clips, insulating mounts and removable service access. Main 6mm2 cables must have broad bends, not tight hairpins. No conductive bare power contacts casually exposed near bodywork.
These are sizable components: use proportions of a small workshop robot roughly430mm long and300mm wide overall, low ground clearance for a flat indoor floor, rather than magically miniaturizing the electrical hardware. This envelope is exploratory and must NOT appear as a certified dimension. Leave realistic clearances for front-wheel steering and rear gears. Everything is DIY fabrication from cut plates, simple folded sides or bolted rails, not a commercial RC chassis. No external battery charger, no charging brick or tools mounted on the vehicle. No futuristic cosmetic equipment. Do not imply the image is a dimensionally verified CAD assembly.
Composition: one concept only, no collage, no alternatives in this image. Chassis dominates frame with all four wheels fully visible. Use an elevated view that reveals the packaging; any service lid may be lifted slightly or ghosted solely to reveal hidden hardware, never duplicate components. Add just a tasteful French title at top and the exact small footer "Concept visuel - implantation à valider". No dimension lines, no fabricated performance claims, no brands or invented readable PCB circuit labels.

variants.name: Plateau ouvert
variants.detail: Title verbatim: "A - PLATEAU OUVERT". A broad, flat grey aluminium CNC-cut lower plate with rounded perimeter and front steering relief cutouts. Open serviceable construction, no enclosing shell. Battery low along the centreline. Two rear motor/reduction modules symmetrically placed, visible guarded gears. A small removable electronics bridge above the middle/front battery area carries Pi and regulator, while the bulky power protection occupies separate lower side zones. Heatsink fins open to outside air on a side edge; power-cutoff accessible from above. Simple low front camera bracket and rounded front bumper. This is the simplest inspectable plate construction, deliberately visibly different from a central-spine or boxed frame.

variants.name: Poutre centrale et modules latéraux
variants.detail: Title verbatim: "B - POUTRE CENTRALE". A visibly narrow longitudinal structural spine/tray with the battery low inside its central channel, bolted front and rear crossmembers, and TWO wide removable side-pod mounting trays flanking the spine. Side trays are functional and visibly separate from the central backbone: one contains covered power distribution/fuses/cutoff, the other cooled relay and rear-associated electronics; Pi on a short accessible bridge with antenna unobstructed. Rear motor/reduction brackets bolt to the rear crossmember, front servo and tie rods to the front crossmember. Open undercut spaces between pods and axle modules; a central rib is visually dominant. Guarded spur gears and no belts. Overall footprint still large enough for all selected industrial power hardware; no cartoon narrow motorcycle chassis.

variants.name: Bac à deux niveaux

Main battery and heavy electrical power protection are LOW in the tray; Pi, regulator and camera connection are on the upper protected tray. Show upper tray partially open or with one translucent service-cover section so distinct lower components remain understandable without an exploded assembly. Ventilation slots and a side-exposed heatsink; no sealed hot box. Power cutoff protrudes accessibly through side flange. A modest integrated nose protects the front board camera; clear front-wheel steering cutouts. This is the cleanest protected two-storey enclosure, not a tall cage and not a generic racing-car body.

variants.name: Cadre modulaire boulonné
variants.detail: Title verbatim: "D - CADRE MODULAIRE". A clearly visible bolted ladder frame made from two straight aluminium longitudinal rails and several removable crossmembers, with modular flat equipment cassettes and slotted brackets. Distinct rectangular battery cradle very low between the rails, removable power-electrics cassette along one side, separately ventilated relay/heatsink bracket, removable Pi/camera electronics cassette. Front steering mechanism on a replaceable front axle plate; the two independent rear motor/spur-reduction modules on separate rear plates. Large components are placed in open accessible bays, cables follow clips along rail edges. A low simple protective hoop/bumper at the front, not a full roll cage. Visible bolts, gussets, modularity and straightforward workshop fabrication. No suspension springs. This variant must look like a rail-and-crossmember assembly, not a continuous monocoque plate.
